messages.subject: Turnover Colext
parts:
Dear members,

I`m using the colext function to understand the impact of hurricane Maria in birds and frogs distributions in Puerto Rico.

I`m working with 68 sampling sites, 3 primary visits, and 17 secondary occasions.

I`m having some difficulties to extract the derived parameter "turnover". This is the error that I get when trying to use the function "turnover":


> vignette("colext")
> turnover <- function(fm) {
+   psi.hat <- plogis(coef(fm, type="psi"))
+   if(length(psi.hat) > 1)
+     stop("this function only works if psi is scalar")
+   T <- getData(fm)@numPrimary
+   tau.hat <- numeric(T-1)
+   gamma.hat <- plogis(coef(fm, type="col"))
+   phi.hat <- 1 - plogis(coef(fm, type="ext"))
+   if(length(gamma.hat) != T-1 | length(phi.hat) != T-1)
+     stop("this function only works if gamma and phi T-1 vectors")
+   for(t in 2:T) {
+     psi.hat[t] <- psi.hat[t-1]*phi.hat[t-1] +
+       (1-psi.hat[t-1])*gamma.hat[t-1]
+     tau.hat[t-1] <- gamma.hat[t-1]*(1-psi.hat[t-1]) / psi.hat[t]
+   }
+   return(tau.hat)
+ }

> pb = parboot(fm4, statistic=turnover, nsim=2)

Error in statistic(object, ...) : 
  this function only works if psi is scalar
Called from: statistic(object, ...)

Can anyone help me with this error?

Thank you very much

Best,

Marconi

messages.author: 4f80e1927b0757cb
messages.subject: Re: Turnover Colext
parts:
Marconi,

Looks like that turnover function is expecting a very specific model structure: one where there are no covariates on psi and where colonization and extinction vary  with primary period (as with the vignette example).

If your model fm4 is not structured this way (for example if you have one or more covariates on psi) you will get an error like the one you see.

You would have to adjust the turnover function to correspond to your model depending on what your fm4 model structure looks like, but you haven't given us that.

Ken

}

messages.subject: Re: [unmarked] Re: Turnover Colext
parts:
I think not.  It looks like you just removed the check for whether psi is scalar or not.  You'll need to state an explicit elevation (or more likely look at several elevations).

I'm guessing that elev is a continuous variable.  If so, then coef(fm, type="psi") should give you two parameters: one for the slope and one for an intercept.  From those two parameter estimates you'll construct the associated psi value for a specified elevation.  If you set elev <- 1000, then you might want to use

psi.hat <- plogis(sum(coef(fm, type="psi")*c(1,elev)))

in the turnover function for each elevation of interest.

Jim
